pages.title: Build for Warmth
pages.text: Seal the room, then insulate its floor, walls and roof. Airtightness and insulation are separate: a full glass wall can seal air while losing heat readily.$(br2)Wool, snow blocks and moss insulate well. Wood loses less heat than stone. Ordinary glass, metal and ice are poor insulators. $(l:heating/insulated_glass)Insulated Glass$(/l) is an insulating window.

pages.title: Layers and Size
pages.text: Up to three layers outward from each room boundary combine their insulation. Layer the floor and roof as well as walls. Thin windows can dominate losses in an otherwise warm base.$(br2)Small rooms heat quickly; large rooms and heavy structures take longer. Better insulation saves fuel at the same target. It does not produce heat.$(br2)$(italic)ORSA recommends fewer windows than an aquarium.$()

pages.title: Air and Structure
pages.text: Room air and the physical walls store heat separately. Heaters warm air; air warms the structure. Walls then lose heat to their surroundings.$(br2)After burnout or redstone shutdown, stored heat cools gradually. Warm-up can need much more power than Holding. More heaters or stronger tiers speed warm-up while sharing the same room target.

pages.title: Ground and Depth
pages.text: The surface chills before deep ground. Below the fixed Y 64 reference, the cold front takes time to penetrate; greater depth delays cooling. Above it, the surface and altitude rules apply.$(br2)Deep ground is an intended thermal refuge. Its warmth depends on progression and preset. It does not replace oxygen: late Phase 6 still needs EVA or a sealed room with an oxygen supply.

pages.title: Reading Fuel Estimates
pages.text: Holding 8% means roughly 8% of that heater’s full ordinary burn rate is currently needed. The display averages a few seconds. Remaining time is an estimate at that rate, not a promise.$(br2)Warm-up, target changes, insulation, weather and breaches change demand. Machinery and frostmites can add costs. Judge survival fuel use with the fuel actually inserted; there is no fixed wool/glass runtime ratio.

pages.title: One Room Temperature
pages.text: Heaters, connected Cores and connected fires warm the same stored room air and structure. The thermostat and HUD start from one room temperature, without additional heat bonuses when you walk toward a Core or campfire.$(br2)The heater default is 20°C; a $(l:heating/thermostat)thermostat$(/l) selects 10-30°C. Passive sources can exceed that target, so reduce independent heat or open a heat vent. Personal equipment and status effects can still change your HUD reading.

pages.title: Breach and Recovery
pages.text: A $(l:heating/atmospheric_breach)vacuum breach$(/l) removes room air, while surviving walls keep their heat. Seal every opening and restore oxygen; incoming cold air warms from those walls.$(br2)Without air, sealed burners heat the structure less efficiently. Radiant warmth is only partial protection. Atmosphere restored confirms air, not a warm room. A thermostat controls heaters and same-room heat vents together. Vents need uncovered outdoor faces to reject excess heat.
